description: A three-person startup is building a mobile app that helps neighbours organise small local events: street clean-ups, book swaps, pick-up football. Users create an event, invite people nearby and chat in the event's group. The founders are not sure which features people actually want, so the plan is to put a basic version in front of a few hundred users in one city and change it based on what they do. The founders talk to users every week and expect the feature list to change after almost every round of feedback. They want to ship updates to the app stores every week. The app stores only a display name, an email address and an approximate location for each user; there are no payments. The backend is a standard managed database and serverless functions, which the team has used before. If the app goes down, events are simply organised in other ways for a day. One of the founders acts as product owner and sits with the developer every day, and there is no fixed budget or scope: the seed funding covers about nine months.

phases.name: Inception
phases.objective: Define initial product vision and validate core user needs with early prototypes
activities: Conduct user interviews to identify key event types and user pain points
Define initial feature set based on user feedback from pilot city
Establish product vision and key success metrics with the product owner

approval_gate.criteria: Vision aligns with user needs and has at least 3 confirmed use cases

exit_criteria: Vision document approved and user needs validated

phases.name: Iterations
phases.objective: Develop and test a minimum viable product with regular re-prioritisation of features
activities: Build a basic event creation and chat feature in iterative sprints
Integrate user invite and location-based notification functionality
Conduct weekly user feedback sessions to re-prioritise requirements
deliverables: Working prototype of event creation and chat
Traceability matrix linking features to user needs
testing: Unit testing for core event flow

approval_gate.criteria: At least 70% of users report positive experience with core features

exit_criteria: Core features functional and validated by user feedback

phases.name: Release
phases.objective: Deploy a new version of the app to production with automated rollback capability
activities: Package the updated app with automated deployment scripts
Run automated tests and validate rollback procedure
Deploy to app stores with display name, email, and location data
deliverables: Updated app version in app stores

approval_gate.criteria: App is live, deployment script passes automated tests, and rollback is functional

exit_criteria: App deployed and available to users in pilot city

phases.name: Operate and Improve
phases.objective: Monitor production performance and iterate based on user feedback and usage data
activities: Monitor app performance and user engagement in real time
Respond to incidents within 15 minutes of detection
Conduct weekly review to re-prioritise features based on user feedback
testing: Production monitoring logs and incident reports

approval_gate.criteria: At least 2 new features added or 1 major feature improved in the next iteration

exit_criteria: Next iteration plan approved and scheduled

justification: Agile is ranked first due to high change frequency and low requirement stability, enabling adaptive planning. The runner-up, DevSecOps, fits less well because security risks are low and no security activities are mandated. V-Model is lowest-ranked as it requires fixed requirements and test documentation, contradicting the project's dynamic, evolving nature.
